figures.caption: Figure 2. Illustration of the shortest path (in bold green arrows) between the last RNN cell at site xn and the first site x1 of (a) the vanilla RNN and (b) the dilated RNN given a system size N . For the vanilla RNN, the shortest path between sites separated by lag n is given by O(n), whereas for the dilated RNN, the shortest path has worst-case scaling O(log(n)).
Table I. Hyperparameters used to obtain the results reported in this paper.

Figure 1. Schematic representation of the RNN architectures used. (a) RNN wave function which sequentially generates the conditional probabilities pn and conditional phases ϕn by taking the one-hot encoded spin σn−1 and hidden vector hn−1 as inputs at the nth step. (b) A dilated RNN illustration for a spin configuration with length N = 5. For the nth site, the network uses the hidden vector h (l) n−2l−1 from the (n − 2l−1)th site at the same layer l, in addition to h (l−1) n from the preceding layer. If the dilation length is larger than the spin position n, a zero initialization h0 is used instead.
